title: Crypto bot builders: how do you handle pre-trade scam filtering on fast-moving tokens?
author: Mantisirleuw
selftext:
This is market research, and I'll be upfront that I'm building a tool in this space, so I'm biased. No link here, I'll only share it in a comment if someone asks. Mostly I want to understand what people actually do today.

For anyone running automated strategies on new crypto tokens (Solana especially, but curious about any chain): these tokens can be minutes or seconds old, and a chunk of them are outright traps, liquidity gets pulled, reselling gets blocked. How are you filtering that before you enter?

\- Do you have a pre-trade risk check in your pipeline, or do you rely on position sizing and stops to survive the bad ones?  
\- If you check, what signals do you look at and where do you pull them from?  
\- How much of your losses on these are avoidable filtering problems versus just the nature of the game?  
\- Would you build this in-house, buy it, or not bother?

Trying to figure out if there's a real gap here or if it's already solved for serious players.

comments.author: No-Abbreviations1973
comments.body: There is nothing to win if 99.9% are scams and only 3 a day are legit. All tokens rug, im happy if you prove me wrong.

replies.author: Mantisirleuw
replies.body: you're probably right on the base rate, not gonna argue that. but that's kind of my point: if only 3 a day are legit, finding those 3 is the whole game. since you said prove me wrong, what would actually count as proof for you? a public backtest on labeled rugs, or a feed of verdicts signed and timestamped *before* the rug happens? building the second one because I don't expect anyone to trust accuracy claims on faith.
